notes: Wireless DECT (1.9GHz) / 2.4GHz intercom beltpack, not a wired video/audio-routing device. Riedel's official Bolero Mini brochure (riedel.net/fileadmin/user_upload/Bolero_Mini_2pager.pdf) labels only one physical connector on the beltpack body: a "Hirose HR10 6-pin connector," described elsewhere in the same brochure's marketing copy as a "small push-pull connector." This single port is the combined interface for wired headset audio (mic/earpiece) and USB charging/firmware update, mirroring Riedel's full-size Bolero beltpack (which instead exposes separate 4-pin XLR headset + USB-C charging ports) but condensed into one miniature connector for the Mini's 28mm-thin form factor. HR10 6-pin is not present in the given connector enum, so it is modeled here as the closest available id (xlr4-dc, a small multi-pin circular connector) with usb-c listed under accepts since the port also carries USB charging/data. No grade is set: this is an analog-audio + proprietary-DC/USB combo connector and the brochure states no USB speed. No separate AC/DC power inlet, RJ45, or RF antenna connector is shown on the beltpack itself in the brochure's labeled diagram. Confidence is medium: the brochure explicitly names and diagrams the single HR10 port, but gives no pin-level signal breakdown and does not state a USB version. The companion antenna (BL-ANT-1010) and 5-bay charger dock are separate accessory products not covered by this entry.
